h: לַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב, ה׳ Tu B'Av, 5

p: "There were no festive days for Yisrael
like the fifteenth of Av," and so on.
And in the Gemara they gave reasons
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
why there were no festive days for Yisrael
on the fifteenth of Av — why is it?
that what is said in the Mishnah,
"on the day of the gladness of his heart —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
may it be rebuilt speedily in our days,"
הַמְכוּוָּן עַל בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ דִּלֶעָתִיד
refers to the building of the future Beis HaMikdash,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא (פְּסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא יג, טו)
as they said in the Pesikta (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana 13:15);
and that is why it says,
"may it be rebuilt speedily in our days"
And then there will be the essential
and this is why it says "the gladness of his heart,"
along the lines of what they said
"To My heart I revealed it," and so on.
and it says in Pri Etz Chaim of the Arizal
and this is based on what it says
and it says in the holy Zohar
by the Holy One, blessed is He,
in His Garden of Delights," and so on,
from the aspect of the Written Torah,
to the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לַהּ.
"the mouth — we call it Torah she'b'al peh"
"the day on which those killed at Beitar were given over for burial"
even though this was after the Destruction,
whereas the Mishnah speaks of the time of the Beis HaMikdash,
as they said in the Baraisa
בַּת מֶלֶךְ שׁוֹאֶלֶת מִבַּת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.
"The king's daughter would borrow from the Kohen Gadol's daughter."
that it is a day prepared for this holiness.
And Beitar was the kingdom of Ben Koziva,
and it says in the Midrash
"said: This is the King Mashiach," and so on.
since Rabbi Akiva erred about him,
he was in truth fit for it.
That is, there was in him
something of the light of Torah she'b'al peh;
who was the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
said of him, "This is the King Mashiach."
And this is the meaning of
what the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote
And we find in the Midrash Rabbah there
that he said, when he went out to war,
"Do not help us and do not shame us";
"Have You not, O G-d, forsaken us," etc.
it says that Bar Daroma said this,
David was saying it in astonishment."
And from the wording of the Midrash Rabbah,
הָדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב הֲלֹא אַתָּה וְגוֹ׳
"this is what is written: Have You not," etc.,
it appears that the truth was with him
But in truth he knew within himself
that he was fit for redemption,
שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כָּל כָּךְ
for there was so much light of Torah she'b'al peh in him,
which is the essential rectification in the exiles;
שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה הַשְּׁבוּעָה
that he did not know that it was about this that the oath was made,
"that they should not go up as a wall,"
even if they should be fit for redemption;
along the lines of what they said
"'I am a wall' — this is Torah";
"that they should not go up as a wall,"
that is, by the power of the "wall," which is Torah;
and for that reason he was killed.
And possibly he was Mashiach ben Yosef,
and for this reason he was killed.
And possibly he was of the family of Yosef
and of the family of David —
from one through the males and from the other through the females.
And Mashiach ben David can be
even one who is only through the females
he is such as Rabbeinu HaKadosh";
וְאִין סָלִיק רַב הוּנָא רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְהָכָא
"And if Rav Huna the Exilarch came up here,
and he is from the males
and I am from the females," and so on.
that Ben Koziva was from both families,
that he was Mashiach ben David,
while in truth he was Mashiach ben Yosef,
And afterward, on the fifteenth of Av,
when those killed at Beitar were given over for burial,
they understood that the corruption had been rectified
and therefore they then instituted in Yavneh
"For I have given you a good teaching,"
which refers to the Written Torah;
and "VeHaMeitiv" alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
"The Torah of Your mouth is good for me";
this is a Torah of kindness";
"And a Torah of kindness is on her tongue" —
like a fence in the vineyard
But according to what has been said, it may be
that wine alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
as it is written in the Raaya Mehemna
and drink of the wine I have mixed' —
this is the bread of the Written Torah
and the wine of the Oral Torah."
"From here on, one who adds will have life added to him";
and it speaks of one who is constantly occupied with Torah
and from the fifteenth of Av
he must add also at night.
which is the aspect of the moon,
which receives from the Written Torah.
when it was day," and so on,
"and when He would teach him orally,
he knew that it was night," and so on.
And it says in the Gemara
"The moon was created only for girsa" —
And this is the meaning of what is said in Eichah
"Arise, cry out in the night," etc.
There only lamentations and moaning are spoken;
how then does it say in the middle, "Arise, sing out"?
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
But it is based on what they said in the Midrash
אֵין רִנָּה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה
"There is no song of Torah except at night,
as it says, 'Arise, sing out in the night'";
that is, to review the recitation of the Mishnayos,
which they were accustomed to learn with a melody
so that they would not forget,
because they would learn them by heart,
"and one who learns without a melody";
"Learn the received teaching, and let it be like a song" —
for one who states a thing without its reason,
And this is the meaning of
"the moon was created only for girsa":
And this is from the fifteenth of Av on,
for of the time before it the Gemara said
"The night was created only for sleep";
such as the nights of the Tammuz season.
that the measure of sixty breaths
and from the fifteenth of Av on,
when the night is longer than six hours,
one must add from the night onto the day,
"The moon was created only for girsa."
And this is what is said in Eichah,
הַמְכוּוָּן עַל לִימּוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
which refers to the study of Torah she'b'al peh;
for this will be the rectification in exile,
since the essence of exile is
in order to extract from there
And when they have extracted all of Torah she'b'al peh,
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה שָׂרִיד לְבֵית עֵשָׂו וְגוֹ׳
"And there shall be no survivor of the house of Esav," etc.
וְכֵן תָּמִיד יֶאֱרַע חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב
And so the fifteenth of Av always falls
in the days before or after
in which is said the passage "When you beget"
and after that the second Commandments;
as it says in the Midrash
"And in the second Tablets I give you
that there be in them halachos, Midrash and aggados."
And when it falls on that Shabbos itself,
it is certainly a time suited
for the spreading of Torah she'b'al peh;
as we said the meaning of
"Comfort, comfort My people, says your G-d"
that the entire purpose of the exiles
is only to extract from them
of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh within them,
And this is what they said in the Mishnah:
"There were no festive days for Yisrael
כַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב וּכְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וְכוּלֵּי
like the fifteenth of Av and Yom HaKippurim," and so on;
שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם מֵעִנְיַן בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for both pertain to the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh:
the day on which the second Tablets were given,
שֶׁכָּלוּל בָּהֶם גַּם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
in which Torah she'b'al peh is also included;
and likewise the fifteenth of Av
is a time suited for adding
in Torah she'b'al peh, as mentioned above.
And it says, "And so it says:
'Go out and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon,
that is, upon the King to Whom peace belongs;
"upon the crown with which his mother crowned him" —
as Rashi, of blessed memory, explained.
And this is based on what it says
"A woman of valor is the crown of her husband";
and this is why the Gemara brings in connection with this
"In the future the Holy One, blessed is He,
will make a dance for the tzaddikim,
וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב בֵּינֵיהֶם בְּגַן עֵדֶן וְכוּלֵּי
and He will sit among them in Gan Eden," and so on;
that is, they will be like a crown
for the Holy One, blessed is He.
And this is "the crown with which his mother crowned him,"
is the aspect of Knesses Yisrael.
And so the souls of Yisrael will surround,
as it says, "the crown of her husband";
and this is the secret of "a woman shall surround a man"
